crm_notes:
Summary: Mid-market multi-tenant SaaS (agent platform) evaluating Redwood Hosted API for initial POC, with clear intent to move to Dedicated for tenant isolation and predictable throughput. Main evaluation axes: streaming stability during long-running tool calls, per-tenant rate limits/quotas, and first-token latency SLOs.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-02-12: Intro call (AE Jenna) — overview of platform, product fit looks strong (multi-tenant agents for SMB/SME customers).
- 2026-02-18: Hosted API demo (streaming + tool calling) — ran live demo with tool-call example (calendar lookup). Customer quote: "can't have stream drops during tool calls — our UX collapses."
- 2026-02-20: Security checklist submitted (SAML, audit logs, KMS). Legal flagged residency reqs for EU customers.
- 2026-02-25: Security deep-dive w/ Marco (SE) — discussed VPC options and Dedicated isolation.
- 2026-02-26: POC kickoff (hosted) — 2-week POC to validate streaming stability & per-tenant throttling. Synthetic load scripts provided.
- 2026-03-01: Mid-poc check-in — streaming spikes caused 2 reconnects under concurrent tool calls (investigating backlog/backpressure).

POC details / technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workload: multi-tenant chat/agent platform; many tenants with variable burst patterns.
- Target SLOs: First-byte/first-token latency target ~ 200-350ms for short turns; steady-state per-token latency target ~ 20-40ms; 95th p95 token streaming latency goal 400ms.
- Concurrency expectations: per-tenant concurrent chat sessions typically 5-20; platform peak aggregate concurrency expected ~200-400 concurrent streams during peak events.
- Rate limiting needs: per-tenant quotas (configurable) + global burst guardrails. Want preflight capability to set hard and soft limits per API key/tenant and rate-limit headers for graceful degradation.
- Streaming stability: must tolerate external tool call latencies (webhook/blocking calls) without dropping the connection; prefer automatic buffering/backpressure handling or fallback to chunked responses.
- Model routing: prefer hosted for fast iteration; Dedicated for guaranteed throughput and data isolation. Need automatic fallback to smaller model variants when dedicated capacity saturated.
- Observability: token-level latency & cost breakdown per tenant, per-route errors, and tracing for tool calls.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Interested in Hosted API to validate integration and UX quickly. Dedicated is priority for procurement (isolation + predictable billing) if POC validates.
- Asking for a pricing worksheet showing committed Dedicated sizing vs. burst pricing on Hosted API.
- ARR expect ~ $50k–$200k first-year; procurement slated for May 2026 if POC passes.

Open questions & blockers:
- Need clear spec for per-tenant rate-limit config surface in API (headers, dashboard, SDK).
- Legal needs confirmation on EU data residency for particular customers — exploring Private/VPC options.
- Streaming reconnect behavior under high concurrency: want recommendations / best practices and mitigation (auto-retry windows, backpressure knobs).

Action items for Redwood team:
- Provide Dedicated sizing template and sample cost scenarios for their expected 200-400 concurrent streams.
- Share recommended rate-limit header conventions and example implementation for tenant-level quotas.
- Run extended streaming stability test during POC week 2 (Mar 8-12) with their synthetic load scripts; capture p50/p95/p99 per-token latencies and reconnect counts.
- Send draft pricing worksheet + contract TL; deck link: drive://redwood/pricing/agentwise-poa

Recent quote (AE notes): "If we get consistent streaming during tool calls and a simple per-tenant quota model, we can justify Dedicated — predictable latency and isolation are the deal-winners."
